partners.mechanism_chain: MFN2 (HGNC:7314) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial dynamics (GO:0007005); PINK1 (HGNC:17053) —DISRUPTS→ mitochondrial dynamics (GO:0007005); mitochondrial dynamics (GO:0007005) —LEADS_TO→ mitophagy (GO:0000024); mitophagy (GO:0000024) —LEADS_TO→ damaged mitochondria (CHEBI:17761); damaged mitochondria (CHEBI:17761) —DISRUPTS→ adipocyte differentiation and proliferation (HP:0000978); damaged mitochondria (CHEBI:17761) —DISRUPTS→ neuronal dysfunction (GO:0000970); adipocyte differentiation and proliferation (HP:0000978) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0007908; neuronal dysfunction (GO:0000970) —LEADS_TO→ MONDO:0011613. Mutations in MFN2 (MSL) and PINK1 (AREOPD6) both impair mitochondrial dynamics and mitophagy. In MSL, MFN2 haploinsufficiency disrupts mitochondrial dynamics, leading to abnormal adipocyte differentiation and proliferation. In AREOPD6, PINK1 loss-of-function mutations impair mitophagy, leading to the accumulation of damaged mitochondria, which in turn causes neuronal dysfunction and Parkinsonism. The shared pathway of mitochondrial quality control (dynamics and mitophagy) acts as the convergence point.

#### 1. frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis 4  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.449)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5205685)

**Proposed mechanism:** MFN2 (HGNC:7508) —DISRUPTS→ Mitochondrial dynamics (GO:0007005); Mitochondrial dynamics (GO:0007005) —LEADS_TO→ Lysosomal function (GO:0005704); Lysosomal function (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Adipocyte differentiation (HP:0004934); Lysosomal function (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Frontotemporal dementia (HP:0001214); Lysosomal function (GO:0005704) —LEADS_TO→ Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (HP:0007210). Mutations in MFN2 disrupt mitochondrial dynamics, which in turn impacts lysosomal function. This disruption in lysosomal function can lead to both aberrant adipocyte differentiation (multiple symmetric lipomatosis) and neurodegeneration (frontotemporal dementia and/or amyotrophic lateral sclerosis).

**How to falsify it:** Absence of functional evidence linking MFN2 dysfunction to impaired lysosomal function, or demonstration that MFN2 variants associated with MSL do not impact lysosomal function, or vice versa for FTD/ALS. _(variant: Common variants (AF > 0.01) in MFN2 in relevant populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of MFN2 in mitochondrial and lysosomal pathways could reveal novel therapeutic targets for both metabolic and neurodegenerative disorders.

#### 2. lung cancer  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-5205685)

**Proposed mechanism:** MAP3K8 (HGNC:6857) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP1076); MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP1076) —LEADS_TO→ Adipocyte proliferation (HP:0000979); KRAS (HGNC:6395) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP1076); PIK3CA (HGNC:9534) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP1078); BRAF (HGNC:1097) —INCREASES→ MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP1076); EGFR (HGNC:3430) —INCREASES→ PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP1078); RB1 (HGNC:9897) —DISRUPTS→ Cell cycle regulation (WP:WP177); PI3K-Akt signaling pathway (WP:WP1078) —INCREASES→ Cell cycle regulation (WP:WP177); MAPK signaling pathway (WP:WP1076) —INCREASES→ Cell cycle regulation (WP:WP177); Cell cycle regulation (WP:WP177) —LEADS_TO→ Lung cancer (MONDO:0008903). Gain-of-function mutations in MAP3K8 can activate the MAPK signaling pathway, contributing to adipocyte proliferation in multiple symmetric lipomatosis. Concurrently, oncogenic mutations in KRAS, BRAF, and EGFR can activate the MAPK pathway, while mutations in PIK3CA activate the PI3K-Akt pathway. Both pathways converge to dysregulate cell cycle control, with RB1 loss-of-function further exacerbating this, ultimately leading to lung cancer.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that the specific activating mutations in MAP3K8 found in multiple symmetric lipomatosis patients do not lead to downstream signaling activation in relevant cell types, or that common lung cancer driver mutations do not impact cell cycle progression. _(variant: N/A)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting common downstream signaling pathways like MAPK and PI3K-Akt, or cell cycle regulators, could offer therapeutic strategies for both multiple symmetric lipomatosis and lung cancer, particularly for patients with specific genetic alterations.
